top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Russia's overnight ballistic-missile and drone barrage on Kyiv killed at least 15 people and destroyed a nine-storey apartment block, with Ukrainian officials saying the capital now has almost no interceptors left to stop ballistic missiles. Money was the other big story of the day: US gross national debt crossed US$40 trillion for the first time, months ahead of forecasts, and Asian markets only steadied after the Treasury stepped in to pull bond yields back down. Asia supplied the rest - North Korea fired more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles as the Ulchi Freedom Shield drills wind down, and a Chinese court jailed Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan for life. Accountability cases ran in parallel across three continents, from Israel's reversal over the killing of Hind Rajab to the first extradition of an Assad-era officer to Syria. Watch whether Trump's threatened 'economic warfare' on Iran and anyone trading with it turns into an actual sanctions list, because nothing has been published yet.

stories.headline: Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills at least 15; Ukraine says its air defences are running dry
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Ukraine's air force said Russia fired dozens of missiles and 168 drones and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90 per cent of drones were downed, but officials said the city is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of a shortage of interceptors. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

stories.headline: US national debt passes US$40 trillion for the first time
stories.summary: US Treasury data showed the gross national debt crossing US$40 trillion, reaching about US$40.05 trillion - a milestone reached months earlier than forecasters expected and only five months after the debt passed US$39 trillion. Rising interest costs, social security and health obligations, and a US$432 billion July deficit swollen by refunds of tariffs struck down in court all contributed.

stories.headline: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan jailed for life; company fined more than US$2 billion
stories.summary: A Chinese court sentenced Hui Ka Yan, founder of collapsed property giant Evergrande, to life in prison and fined the company more than US$2 billion. Evergrande's default in 2021 triggered the wider Chinese property downturn; analysts say the sentence draws a line under the case but does little on its own to revive the sector.

stories.headline: North Korea fires more than 10 ballistic missiles as US-South Korea drills wind down
stories.summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea launched more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area towards the sea east of the peninsula, flying about 300km. Japan's coastguard said a missile fell outside its exclusive economic zone. Seoul's presidential office called the launch a grave violation of UN Security Council resolutions and ordered the military to maintain readiness as the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise with the US nears its end.

stories.headline: Trump threatens 'economic warfare' on Iran and on any country that helps it
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he would impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warned that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government bodies give Tehran a lifeline would face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published, so the scope remains a threat rather than a measure. Iranian officials responded dismissively, and Tehran's military said separately it is ready to conduct offensive strikes as talks stall.

stories.headline: Trump says he will meet Kim Jong Un this year; Kim's sister says she is unaware of any contact
stories.summary: Trump said he expects to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un later this year. Kim Yo Jong, the leader's sister, said she was unaware of any contact between the two sides. Separately, South Korea's military estimated North Korea holds up to 120 nuclear warheads, well above the figure Trump has cited publicly.

stories.headline: Ecuador's intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash
stories.summary: A helicopter crash in Kenya killed Ecuador's intelligence chief along with five American nationals, according to officials cited by the BBC. The circumstances of the crash and the purpose of the flight have not been officially detailed.

stories.headline: Four railway workers killed by a train in Japan
stories.summary: Four workers were struck and killed by a train in Japan, according to Japanese authorities cited by the BBC and CNA. The workers were on the tracks at the time; an investigation into how the train came to be running on the section is under way.

stories.headline: Assad-era officer extradited to Syria on war crimes charges in a first
stories.summary: An officer from the deposed Assad government has been extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges - the first such extradition since Assad's fall, according to the BBC. Lebanon separately handed a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus under an arrest warrant. Syria's new authorities have said they intend to try officials of the former government domestically.

stories.headline: Israel opens bidding for a contested West Bank settlement project; Britain plans sanctions
stories.summary: Israel has opened tenders for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister said he plans sanctions over Israeli settlement expansion, and the US ambassador to Israel warned settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans. Israel maintains the project is lawful; most of the international community regards settlements in occupied territory as illegal under international law, a position Israel disputes.

stories.headline: Israel confirms its soldiers fired on the car in which Hind Rajab was killed, opens criminal inquiry
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed its soldiers fired at the vehicle in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opened a criminal investigation. Her family said it does not trust the Israeli judiciary to deliver accountability.

stories.headline: Australia says it is 'outraged' as Israel declines to prosecute over aid worker's killing
stories.summary: Canberra said it was outraged after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen worker in Gaza. The decision came the same day Israel opened a criminal inquiry into the Hind Rajab case, a contrast Australian officials pointed to.

stories.headline: Anwar says Taiwan is part of China and he would use force to protect Malaysia's unity; Beijing commends, Taipei rebukes
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Taiwan is part of China and that he would also use force to protect Malaysia's territorial unity. Beijing publicly commended the remarks; Taiwan's foreign ministry rebuked them. Malaysia has long held a One China position, but the explicit framing around the use of force is a sharper formulation than Kuala Lumpur usually offers.

stories.headline: Anwar orders investigation into a unit of Malaysia's sovereign wealth fund
stories.summary: Malaysia's prime minister ordered a probe into a subsidiary of state sovereign wealth fund Khazanah Nasional. The government has not published the allegations under investigation or named individuals.

stories.headline: Second arrest in Nord Stream investigation: Ukrainian man detained in Croatia
stories.summary: German prosecutors said a Ukrainian man was arrested in Croatia in connection with the 2022 sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not published the alleged role of the suspect, and no trial date has been set.

stories.headline: Sacked Ukrainian defence minister calls for a wartime election; Kremlin says it shows splits in Kyiv
stories.summary: Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as Ukraine's defence minister, called for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since 2022. The Kremlin said the call showed divisions in Kyiv; Ukrainian officials note that wartime elections are constrained by martial law. Protests in Kyiv have backed Fedorov's demand.

stories.headline: Asian stocks rally after the US Treasury moves to ease bond-market fears
stories.summary: Asian equities rallied and the dollar weakened after the US Treasury intervened to bring down longer-term bond yields, which had jumped as the debt milestone approached. The move steadied a market that had been unsettled for several sessions.

stories.headline: US and Canada say they are close to a final trade deal
stories.summary: Officials in Washington and Ottawa said the two countries are close to concluding a final trade agreement, after months of tariff disputes. Neither side has published the terms or a signing date.

stories.headline: China charges 17 over a Myanmar-based trafficking ring that targeted Chinese citizens
stories.summary: Chinese prosecutors charged 17 members of a human trafficking ring based in Myanmar accused of targeting Chinese nationals, part of a continuing crackdown on scam and trafficking compounds along the Myanmar border.

stories.headline: Poland arrests man over alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian arms industry official
stories.summary: Polish authorities said they arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not publicly named the suspect or the intended target, and no charges have been detailed.

stories.headline: Ex-Zambian minister killed in a security raid on the opposition
stories.summary: A former Zambian government minister was killed during a security operation targeting the opposition, the BBC reported. Zambian authorities have not published a full account of the raid, and opposition figures have called for an independent investigation.

stories.headline: Granada closes the Alhambra after a fresh earthquake
stories.summary: Spanish authorities shut the Alhambra palace complex in Granada after another earthquake struck the area. No serious injuries were reported; the closure is precautionary while the site is inspected.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Police say victims have lost nearly S$2.2 million to impersonation scams run over iMessage in under two months, the sharpest thing in today's Singapore news for anyone with a phone. The rest of the hard news is administrative and consumer-facing: a refreshed Singapore Arrival Card with 19 languages and passport-scan autofill, Causeway Link's cross-border buses from Newton and Queen Street going cashless from today, and bridal chain Korea Artiz Studio losing its Carlton Hotel premises after stopping operations over unpaid wages, leaving couples with paid deposits in limbo. The courts had a heavy day, from a jewellery-store worker jailed for swopping gold with Taobao copies to a sexual assault trial opening. The talk of the town is unusually warm-hearted - two separate bystander-CPR rescues in one day, and a man handing out free earphones to commuters blasting audio on the MRT. If you have a wedding package or a deposit with a bridal studio, check now whether you paid by card or instalment.

stories.headline: Singapore Arrival Card gets a refreshed interface, 19 language options and passport-scan autofill
stories.summary: ICA is rolling out an updated Singapore Arrival Card with a redesigned interface, more language options and the ability to autofill personal details by scanning a passport's biodata page. The card remains free and must be submitted within three days before arrival; ICA has repeated its warning about third-party sites that charge for the service.

stories.headline: Nearly S$2.2 million lost to iMessage impersonation scams in under two months
stories.summary: Police said victims have lost close to S$2.2 million to impersonation scams run over Apple's iMessage in less than two months. Scammers pose as officials or delivery services and move victims to messaging apps before requesting transfers. Police advise enabling the filter for unknown senders and verifying any official-sounding request through a published agency number.

stories.headline: Cross-border Causeway Link buses from Newton and Queen Street go cashless from today
stories.summary: Causeway Link's cross-border services from Newton Food Centre and Queen Street terminals stopped accepting cash from 20 August, moving to card and e-payment only from today. The operator announced the switch the day before it took effect; commuters heading to Johor on these routes need a stored-value or bank card.

stories.headline: Singapore and India agree to deepen cooperation on semiconductors, food safety and telecoms
stories.summary: Ministers from Singapore and India met and agreed to expand cooperation across semiconductors, food security and safety, and telecommunications consumer protection, exchanging best practices in each area. The talks build on the two countries' ministerial roundtable framework.

stories.headline: Police looking into iron ore trader Radiant World
stories.summary: Singapore police confirmed they are looking into iron ore trading firm Radiant World. Police did not detail the nature of the inquiry, and no charges have been announced.

stories.headline: Suspected illegal short-stay and overcrowded rental cases are rising
stories.summary: CNA reported a rise in suspected illegal accommodation cases in Singapore, including units let out for stays shorter than the legal minimum and flats housing more occupants than permitted. Private homes carry a three-month minimum stay and HDB flats six months; breaches can draw fines and, for repeat offenders, prosecution.

stories.headline: Law Society to release its workplace culture audit report after redaction
stories.summary: The Law Society said it will publish the audit report into workplace issues once a redaction process is complete. The society has not given a release date. The audit followed complaints about workplace culture within the organisation.

stories.headline: Two Court of Appeal judges to retire; Family Justice Courts appointment extended
stories.summary: Two Court of Appeal judges will retire, and a Family Justice Courts judge's appointment has been extended, according to announcements reported by The Straits Times. The changes take effect on dates set out in the official notifications.

stories.headline: Korea Artiz Studio's premises taken back by hotel after bridal chain stops operating
stories.summary: Carlton Hotel has taken back the space occupied by bridal chain Korea Artiz Studio after the business stopped operations over unpaid wages, leaving engaged couples who had paid deposits in limbo. CASE has been contacted by affected customers; couples with outstanding packages have been advised to file claims and check whether payments were made by card or instalment.

stories.headline: MOM taps a migrant worker network for early alerts on salary claims and other issues
stories.summary: Minister of State Dinesh Vasu Dash said the Manpower Ministry is using a network of migrant workers to surface problems such as salary claims earlier. The approach is intended to shorten the time between a problem arising and MOM being alerted.

stories.headline: Director of firms in the 400-unpaid-workers case declared bankrupt
stories.summary: The director of companies at the centre of a case involving about 400 unpaid workers has been declared bankrupt, The Straits Times reported. The bankruptcy affects the prospects of recovering outstanding wages through the companies.

stories.headline: Yishun jewellery store employee jailed more than two years for swopping gold with Taobao copies
stories.summary: An employee at a Yishun jewellery store who replaced gold pieces with lookalike items bought from Taobao was jailed for more than two years. The court heard the substitutions went undetected for a period before the store discovered the discrepancy.

stories.headline: Man jailed 21 months for stomping on his 72-year-old father's chest
stories.summary: A man was jailed for 21 months for stomping on his 72-year-old father's chest and fracturing his ribs. The court heard the assault followed a dispute at home.

stories.headline: Trial opens for man accused of sexually assaulting a 16-year-old in an Admiralty Park toilet
stories.summary: The trial began of a man accused of sexually assaulting a 16-year-old girl in a female toilet at Admiralty Park. The accused contests the charges; proceedings are continuing.

stories.headline: Motorcyclist arrested after fleeing a police roadblock and crashing in Farrer Road
stories.summary: A motorcyclist was arrested after failing to stop at a police roadblock and getting into an accident in Farrer Road. Police said investigations are ongoing.

stories.headline: Town council files police report after boys allegedly got into a Woodlands lift shaft
stories.summary: A town council filed a police report after boys allegedly accessed an HDB lift shaft in Woodlands. The town council said the act put the children at serious risk and could damage lift equipment.

stories.headline: Man taken to hospital after a fire in a Buangkok HDB flat
stories.summary: SCDF took a man to hospital after a fire at an HDB flat in Buangkok. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

stories.headline: NAFA campus wing evacuated after a workshop fire; no injuries
stories.summary: A fire in a workshop at the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts led to the evacuation of a campus wing. SCDF put out the blaze and no injuries were reported.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on a missing 77-year-old man last seen in Bukit Merah
stories.summary: Police are seeking information on a 77-year-old man last seen in Bukit Merah. Anyone with information is asked to call the police hotline on 1800-255-0000 or submit it online.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on a missing 15-year-old girl last seen at Lorong Napiri
stories.summary: Police issued an appeal for information on a 15-year-old girl last seen at Block 3 Lorong Napiri. Anyone with information is asked to contact the police.

stories.headline: ComfortDelGro puts S$10 million into BYD electric and hybrid cars for its private-hire fleet
stories.summary: ComfortDelGro is investing S$10 million in BYD electric and hybrid vehicles for its private-hire fleet, continuing the operator's shift away from internal-combustion cars. The vehicles will be added over the coming period.

stories.headline: Tuas Power to build a hydrogen-ready power plant by 2031
stories.summary: Tuas Power will build a hydrogen-ready generation plant targeted for completion by 2031, part of Singapore's plan to keep the option of low-carbon fuels open as the grid is renewed. The plant will initially run on natural gas with the capability to switch to hydrogen blends.

stories.headline: NCSS to spend S$5.6 million to expand help for gaming, pornography and gambling addiction
stories.summary: The National Council of Social Service will spend S$5.6 million to get more agencies treating people with gaming, pornography and gambling addictions, broadening the number of places where help is available.

stories.headline: Four primary schools have ended the parent volunteer scheme for P1 admission priority
stories.summary: Four Singapore primary schools have stopped offering the parent volunteer route that gives priority in Primary 1 registration. Parents relying on the scheme at those schools will need to register through other phases.

stories.headline: New South East CDC scheme pairs residents with people rather than portals
stories.summary: A new South East CDC scheme connects residents to a person who helps them navigate available support, instead of leaving them to find schemes themselves. It targets households that qualify for help but do not apply.

stories.headline: 2,000 tech roles curated for fresh graduates and career switchers
stories.summary: A curated list of about 2,000 technology roles has been put together for fresh graduates and workers looking to upskill or switch careers. The listings span software, data and infrastructure roles.

stories.headline: Co-living is becoming a housing option for young adults, but cost and unfamiliarity hold it back
stories.summary: CNA reported that co-living is emerging as a rental option for young adults in Singapore, while affordability and unfamiliarity with the format remain the main barriers. Operators say demand is growing among singles who do not qualify for public housing yet.

stories.headline: Scoot adds flights to Guiyang, expanding its China network
stories.summary: Scoot will launch flights to Guiyang in south-western China, adding another point to its China network. Booking and start dates were published with the announcement.

stories.headline: SBS Transit staff and commuters perform CPR on a man who collapsed at Woodleigh MRT
stories.summary: Staff and fellow commuters gave CPR to a man who collapsed at Woodleigh MRT station before paramedics arrived. SBS Transit shared the account, which drew widespread praise online.

stories.headline: Man, 53, performs CPR for 10 minutes after witnessing a Seletar West Link accident
stories.summary: A 53-year-old man who witnessed an accident along Seletar West Link performed CPR for about 10 minutes on a casualty before help arrived. It is the second bystander-CPR story circulating in Singapore in a single day.

stories.headline: Man, 57, hands out free earphones to commuters playing loud audio on public transport
stories.summary: A 57-year-old Singaporean has taken to offering free earphones to commuters playing music or videos out loud on buses and trains, an approach that has been widely shared and debated online.

stories.headline: Restored 1982 Toyota Corolla styled like a Hong Kong taxi listed for S$168,888
stories.summary: A restored 1982 Toyota Corolla done up to resemble a Hong Kong taxi is on sale in Singapore for S$168,888, a price that has drawn attention given the car's age and the COE component of any local listing.

stories.headline: Starbucks Singapore's Mofusand collaboration merchandise lands on Aug 25
stories.summary: Starbucks Singapore will release a collection of merchandise from its collaboration with Japanese cat illustration brand Mofusand on 25 August. Previous character collaborations have drawn queues at outlets.

stories.headline: Banker-turned-hawker sells S$7 New York-style Levain cookies at Golden Mile Food Centre
stories.summary: A former banker now runs a stall at Golden Mile Food Centre selling thick New York Levain-style cookies at S$7 each. The stall has become a talking point for its pricing and for the career switch behind it.

stories.headline: Robot at Little India MRT station gives directions and travel information
stories.summary: A robot deployed at Little India MRT station can help commuters find their way and provide travel information, part of a trial of service robots in stations.

stories.headline: Myths and legends take over the Bras Basah.Bugis precinct
stories.summary: A programme of installations and events themed on myths and legends has opened across the Bras Basah.Bugis precinct, with activities at museums and public spaces in the area.

stories.headline: S$54,000 raised for rower Joan Poh's world championship bid as athlete funding gaps persist
stories.summary: A fundraising drive collected S$54,000 to support Olympian rower Joan Poh's bid at the World Rowing Championships. CNA reported that funding remains a recurring hurdle for Singapore athletes in less commercially supported sports.

stories.headline: Loh Kean Yew exits the BWF World Championships in the round of 16
stories.summary: Singapore's Loh Kean Yew was knocked out of the BWF World Championships in the round of 16, losing to Canada's Victor Lai. Loh won the world title in 2021.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Kyiv absorbed the heaviest blow of the day, and what it exposed matters more than the strike itself: Ukraine's air force downed nearly 90% of 168 drones but says the capital has almost nothing left to stop ballistic missiles. Nobody escalated on the ground anywhere else. The Iran theatre stayed rhetorical - Trump threatening consequences for any country that gives Tehran a lifeline, Tehran deriding it, and neither side moving - while the Israel front shifted to courtrooms and land, with the military reversing its account of the Hind Rajab killing and new West Bank settlement tenders drawing a British sanctions threat. The one place genuinely heating up is Syria, where Israel and Turkey are now trading warnings after the Abu al-Duhur airbase strike. Watch the interceptor supply to Kyiv: it is the variable that decides how bad the next barrage is.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: The air war did the day's damage. Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv that destroyed a nine-storey block in Solomianskyi district and damaged a children's hospital and a school; the toll climbed through the day from an initial five, and Moscow has not addressed it. Ukraine's air force says most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of 168 drones were downed but that the city has almost nothing left to stop ballistic missiles. Politically, sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election is now the sharpest domestic challenge to Zelensky since 2022, and the Kremlin has begun using it to argue Kyiv is split. Around the edges: a second Nord Stream arrest in Croatia, a Polish arrest over an alleged plot against a Ukrainian arms official, and a marine drone destroyed near Romania's Neptun Deep. Black Sea grain exports remain near zero and no ceasefire track is running.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.
At least 13 people are killed in a Ukrainian drone strike deep inside Russia, according to Russian officials. The claim has not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia is using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine. Moscow and Pyongyang have not confirmed the claim.
Major Russian grain export terminals are hit in a Ukrainian attack on a Black Sea port, extending the campaign against Russian export infrastructure.
Russia dismisses the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire, saying it sees no grounds for 'half-measures' that would give the other side a respite.
NATO jets shoot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the latest spillover of the air war into alliance territory.
Russia's defence ministry says its summer campaign has resulted in the capture of 19 settlements in southeastern Ukraine. Kyiv has not confirmed the claim.
Ukraine's General Staff says long-range strikes hit the Progress Rocket Space Centre in Samara, some 900km inside Russia, and a military airfield.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Washington keeps escalating economically while the military picture stays frozen. Trump has promised tougher measures and warned that any country whose banks, businesses, airports or government bodies give Tehran a lifeline will face consequences - but with no sanctions list and no named target, it is still a threat rather than a measure, and Iranian officials have answered with derision. Tehran's military says it is ready to conduct offensive strikes, a claim it has not backed with action. The concrete pressure is elsewhere: 17 Iranian nationals charged in the US over an alleged $3.4 billion academic data theft, and a five-agency US warning about AI-generated tooling aimed at Siemens industrial controllers. On the water, The Straits Times reports Iran's grip on Hormuz traffic is slipping without the US having secured it - both sides short of their stated aims.

timeline.event: Iran says a deal with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz is in its final stages.
Houthis reportedly kill six people in their first deadly attack since the start of the Iran war.
Yemen's internationally recognised government says the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha, killing four civilians. The Houthis have not commented.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the US will step up economic pressure on Iran, as two more ships are reported attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Company says one of its vessels came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz the previous day, according to Emirati state media.
Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian', responding to Trump's threat to declare Hormuz US territory.
Yemen's Mocha port suspends commercial and maritime operations after being hit by more than 25 missiles in Houthi attacks over recent days, the port's management says.
Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots, rejecting Tehran's claim that they have been held since Qatari forces downed two Iranian fighter jets.
Iran accuses Qatar of thwarting the investigation into the fate of the three pilots, according to Iranian state-linked media.
Iran's parliament advances a bill further criminalising interviews given to media the state designates as hostile.

Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announces a bounty of about US$30,000 for the killing or capture of US soldiers, saying the plan followed a 'large number of requests' to take part, according to state news agency IRNA.

The US and Iran pass the 60-day deadline set under June's ceasefire memorandum without agreeing a deal on Iran's nuclear programme. Washington has rescinded oil sanctions waivers and reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed.
President Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report carried by CNA.
Iran says it now considers the three missing pilots to be prisoners held in Qatar, saying they went missing during an operation against Al Udeid Air Base. Doha denies holding them.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says the group attacked a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels off Yemen's Mocha with missiles. Riyadh has not confirmed the claim.
Drones target the office of the Iraqi Kurdistan region's prime minister; no casualties are reported and no group has claimed responsibility.
Iran says two French embassy employees have been barred from returning to the country.

Iran threatens to 'go on the offensive' in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails, and says separately it will escalate if Washington does not honour June's memorandum within weeks. The threats are Tehran's own characterisation.
President Trump says Iran will not agree to the deal he believes is needed, and repeats his threat to strike Oman if it obstructs a Hormuz arrangement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urges Trump to pursue talks with Iran and offers Ankara's support in facilitating them.
Government bond yields jump and oil extends gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deadline passes without an agreement, with US stocks having fallen in the previous session on the same combination.

Iranian fishermen begin venturing back into waters near the Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed fighting, an early sign of civilian activity returning to the waterway even as it stays effectively closed to commercial traffic.

Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets Tehran's conditions under the interim deal signed in June. Washington has not publicly responded to the specific terms.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says it received a report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, causing engine-room damage and one crew casualty. No party has claimed the strike.
The United Arab Emirates says its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, both of which fell into the sea. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the statement as 'baseless'.

President Donald Trump says talks with Iran are neither taking place nor scheduled and asserts the Strait of Hormuz is open. Iran says the waterway will stay closed until Washington meets the terms of June's interim deal.
Trump posts a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as US territory, days after Iran's deputy foreign minister said the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
France says it will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days over a July incident involving two staff of the French embassy in Tehran.
The US Justice Department unseals charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute over hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies.

The United Arab Emirates halts all trade and financial dealings with Iran, saying its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory and that Tehran has repeatedly targeted its tankers. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the missile allegation as baseless.
Iran warns Gulf countries against assisting the United States militarily, after the UAE's decision to cut trade ties.

The Straits Times reports that the UAE's financial embargo puts the long-standing Abu Dhabi-Tehran rivalry back in the spotlight, with the UAE having been one of Iran's largest trade and re-export partners.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows further as uncertainty over the waterway's status persists.

The US Justice Department's charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute are reported in full, covering hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies. The defendants are not in US custody.
Iran says its ambassador has met four Iranian nationals detained in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities have not commented publicly.
An Iranian academic detained in the United States over an alleged link to the 1979 hostage crisis writes about conditions in US detention, in an account published by the BBC.

President Donald Trump says on Truth Social that the United States is launching 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' against Iran, saying Tehran failed to take the chance to make a deal. No sanctions list has been published.

Trump warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Iran 'any type of lifeline' will face 'tremendous economic consequences'. The administration has not named which states it means.

The US warns that Siemens programmable logic controllers can be exploited, amid concern that Iranian-linked actors are breaching water treatment plants. CISA has issued advisories; no confirmed compromise of a US utility has been announced.

Analysts tell Al Jazeera that maintenance problems aboard the carrier USS Abraham Lincoln illustrate the limits of sustaining US naval presence through a prolonged Iran conflict. The Navy has not commented on the assessment.

Trump says he will impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Tehran 'any type of lifeline' will face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published.

Iranian officials publicly deride Trump's threat of 'economic warfare'. Separately, Iran's military says it is prepared to conduct offensive strikes as diplomacy with Washington stalls; the statement is Tehran's and has not been independently corroborated.

The Straits Times reports that Iran's practical control over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, while the United States is far from having secured the waterway - leaving both sides short of their stated aims.
The US Justice Department charges 17 Iranian nationals linked to the Mabna Institute over an alleged US$3.4 billion theft of academic and corporate data. The defendants are not in US custody.

US agencies including the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warn that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment operators among the concerns.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Accountability and land, not the front line, drove the day. Israel's military reversed its earlier account and admitted its soldiers fired on the car carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab, opening a criminal investigation - while on the same day Australia said it was outraged that Israel will not prosecute anyone over the killing of an Australian aid worker. Territorially the movement is in the West Bank: Israel has opened bidding on a settlement project critics say would cut the northern West Bank off from the south, Britain says it plans sanctions in response, and the US ambassador has warned settlers off land owned by Palestinian Americans. Strikes on Gaza continued through the day, and Washington has put US$206 million towards a stabilisation force for a peace plan that is still deadlocked. The Syria flank is the one getting hotter: Israel and Turkey are trading warnings after the Abu al-Duhur airbase strike, and an Assad-era officer has been extradited to Damascus for the first time.

timeline.event: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers are killed by an explosion.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel rejects President Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza.
Palestinians are told to leave homes in the West Bank village of Qusra that Israeli settlers had besieged.
Israeli forces block activists attempting to deliver aid to Palestinian families besieged by settlers at Qusra.
US officials say Washington wants Netanyahu to publicly condemn the settler siege at Qusra. Netanyahu has not commented publicly.

Israeli airstrikes on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon kill at least 11 people, Lebanon's health ministry says, in the deadliest day since the June truce. Israel says the strikes targeted Hezbollah.
A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her grandmother tells Al Jazeera the family does not trust the Israeli judiciary.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite Trump's 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked after Netanyahu rejected it on 9 August.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: The DRC Ebola epidemic is now spreading faster outside Ituri than inside it, with confirmed cases roughly doubling week-on-week in North Kivu and Haut-Uele and treatment capacity giving way in some areas. WHO's formal count is already well behind events - its 14 August bulletin was current only to 12 August, and the agency's own Africa situation report adds several hundred more cases and deaths in the four days after that. The response is now also hostage to the conflict: M23 has imposed its own movement restrictions between rebel and government areas after two travellers tested positive, which slows contact tracing as much as it slows spread. Bangladesh's measles emergency keeps adding child deaths daily, while Myanmar's Yangon cholera cluster appears past its admissions peak. For readers outside these regions the practical risk stays low - but WHO still rates the DRC situation very high, and any exported case would be the thing to watch for.

outbreaks.name: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) - DR Congo & Uganda
outbreaks.status: PHEIC in force; largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in DRC and still expanding into new health zones
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO Disease Outbreak News 615 (published 14 Aug), confirmed cases only as of 12 Aug: DR Congo 4,665 cases / 2,184 deaths (CFR 46.8%), Uganda 20 / 2, plus one exported case treated in France and two in Germany. Cases span 54 health zones across six DRC provinces. WHO AFRO External Situation Report 14 (data to 16 Aug) adds a further 640 confirmed cases and 367 deaths beyond Situation Report 13 and puts the crude CFR at 47.4%, so the current total is materially higher than this WHO-confirmed count; the highest weekly figures so far were 579 cases and 304 deaths in week 32 (3-9 Aug). PHEIC declared 17 May 2026; the IHR Emergency Committee met for a second time on 18 Aug.

outbreaks.name: Measles - Bangladesh
outbreaks.status: World's largest measles outbreak by case count; child deaths still accruing daily
outbreaks.scope_note: Bangladesh health authorities' daily bulletin to 8am on 20 Aug: 68 new confirmed cases in 24 hours taking laboratory-confirmed infections to 18,144, and 1,004 new suspected cases taking the suspected total to 146,715; three further deaths took the combined confirmed-plus-suspected toll to 925. Children under five account for about 79% of reported cases. Outbreak began mid-March 2026 and reached WHO via Bangladesh's IHR focal point on 4 April, affecting 58 of 64 districts.

outbreaks.name: Cholera / acute watery diarrhoea - Yangon & Rakhine, Myanmar
outbreaks.status: Yangon admissions past their peak; Rakhine cluster still being traced
outbreaks.cases: 500 hospitalised in Yangon (about 150 rapid-test positive, 9 lab-confirmed); 22 cholera cases in Sittwe
outbreaks.scope_note: Myanmar health ministry figures reported by Bloomberg, Bangkok Post and Khaosod English on 18 Aug: 500 people hospitalised for severe diarrhoea in Yangon, nearly 150 rapid-test positive and nine confirmed as Vibrio cholerae by the National Health Laboratory. Deaths are one in Yangon and two in Sittwe, Rakhine State. The ministry separately reported 82 diarrhoea cases across Rakhine and Mon states as of 15 Aug, including 22 cholera cases in Sittwe. New Yangon admissions have been falling since a one-day peak of more than 100 last week.

stories.headline: Ebola is spreading faster beyond the Congo epicentre, straining the response
stories.summary: Transmission is accelerating outside Ituri province, where the epidemic began. Confirmed cases roughly doubled week-on-week in North Kivu and Haut-Uele, and Tshopo recorded an even larger jump from a smaller base, overwhelming treatment capacity in some areas and stretching contact tracing. The outbreak now covers 54 health zones across six provinces after a first case was confirmed in Bas-Uele.

stories.headline: M23 rebels restrict movement between their territory and government areas over Ebola
stories.summary: The AFC/M23 alliance announced movement restrictions between areas it controls and government-held zones, suspending shared taxis on the Goma-Kirumba road for a month and passenger pirogue routes across Lake Edward. The measures followed two travellers from government-held Lubero testing positive in a village under M23 control. Restrictions imposed by an armed group complicate the formal outbreak response as much as they slow spread.

stories.headline: WHO's latest Ebola bulletin puts confirmed cases at 4,686 and deaths at 2,186
stories.summary: WHO's Disease Outbreak News published on 14 August recorded 4,686 confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths as of 12 August across DR Congo, Uganda and exported cases, a crude case fatality ratio of 46.8% in DRC. WHO said the increase partly reflects stronger surveillance and testing but mostly reflects genuine expansion of the outbreak. An updated risk assessment was being prepared ahead of the IHR Emergency Committee's second meeting on 18 August.

stories.headline: Australia races to vaccinate little penguins against H5N1 bird flu
stories.summary: Australian authorities are moving to shield little penguin colonies from H5N1 as the virus continues its global spread through wild bird populations. Australia had been the last continent without a detected H5N1 incursion in wild birds; the vaccination effort is precautionary conservation work rather than a response to human cases.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch Citrix NetScaler now: an unauthenticated authentication bypass rated 9.3 affects any appliance running a Gateway or AAA virtual server with SAML configured, and Citrix says earlier NetScaler bugs were attacked within days of disclosure. Three flaws are already being exploited in the wild - a Zimbra command-injection RCE that has been patched since July, and an unauthenticated MLflow SSRF that CISA added to its exploited list yesterday - on top of the four macOS, SharePoint, vCenter and Windows IKE bugs added earlier in the week. The web-app tail is unusually heavy this cycle, with critical unauthenticated file-upload-to-RCE bugs in Elementor Pro and Forminator and a GitLab GraphQL flaw that let strangers delete public projects. Everything else is credential theft by other means: Android banking trojans, fake Web3 browser extensions, typosquatted RubyGems and 14,500 hijacked Dahua cameras. If you run internet-facing NetScaler, Zimbra, GitLab or MLflow, treat those four as this week's queue and do them in that order.

stories.headline: Citrix urges immediate patching of two new NetScaler flaws
stories.summary: Citrix issued an advisory for two NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws. CVE-2026-19490 (NVD CVSS 9.3) lets an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass authentication on appliances configured as AAA virtual servers or Gateways with a SAML Action configured; CVE-2026-19489 (CVSS 8.8) is a memory overflow usable for denial of service when SIP ALG is enabled on large-scale NAT groups. Neither is known to be exploited yet, but Citrix noted earlier NetScaler bugs were attacked soon after disclosure. Fixed in 14.1-73.32 and 13.1-63.21 or later.

stories.headline: CISA warns of attacks on a critical MLflow SSRF flaw
stories.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-64849 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 19 August. The flaw is an unauthenticated server-side request forgery in MLflow's webhook test endpoint (POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test) in versions before 3.15.0, rated 9.3 by NVD; attackers are using it to reach cloud metadata services and steal credentials and secrets. Federal agencies face a KEV remediation deadline; anyone running MLflow should upgrade and restrict network access to the tracking server.
stories.source: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News (CISA KEV, NVD)

stories.headline: Elementor Pro flaw lets unauthenticated attackers upload PHP and run code
stories.summary: CVE-2026-32475 (NVD CVSS 9.0) affects Elementor Pro up to 4.2.1. In the Forms module's File Upload field, the extension check and the file-move step run in separate loops, so submitting two file parts for the same field skips the blocklist and writes a PHP file into a public directory. Reported by Tin Pham via Patchstack; fixed in 4.2.2, released 19 August.

stories.headline: Critical Zimbra RCE now actively exploited
stories.summary: CERT Polska reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-73570, a command-injection remote code execution flaw in Zimbra Collaboration Suite that requires the optional zimbra-snmp package to be installed with SNMP notifications enabled. NVD scores it 8.9. Zimbra shipped the fix in 10.1.20 on 20 July 2026, so exposed servers have been unpatched for a month.

stories.headline: NASA AIT-GUI flaws could let unauthenticated attackers issue spacecraft commands
stories.summary: Researchers disclosed flaws in NASA's open-source AIT-GUI ground-software component that could allow unauthenticated attackers to issue spacecraft commands through the tool's interface. AIT-GUI is used in ground segments built on the AMMOS Instrument Toolkit; the risk depends on whether an instance is network-reachable rather than isolated on an operations network.

stories.headline: New 'Manic' Android malware relays stolen data through nearby infected phones
stories.summary: ThreatFabric reported Manic, an Android malware family active since February that combines spyware, banking fraud and remote control, targeting 169 apps with Ukraine as its main focus. It uses transparent overlays to capture keystrokes, and when it cannot reach its command-and-control server directly it exfiltrates data over Wi-Fi Direct or Bluetooth to nearby infected devices, relaying it onward in multi-hop routes - a design that defeats network-level blocking.

stories.headline: ToxicPanda 2.0 and GoldDigger expand Android banking fraud with on-device attacks
stories.summary: Researchers documented new versions of the ToxicPanda and GoldDigger Android banking trojans that carry out on-device fraud - initiating transfers from the victim's own phone rather than exporting credentials - which sidesteps device-fingerprinting controls used by banks.

stories.headline: 40 malicious Firefox extensions posed as Web3 tools to steal wallet secrets
stories.summary: Forty malicious Firefox add-ons impersonating Web3 and crypto-wallet products were found harvesting seed phrases and private keys. Users who installed any wallet extension from an unverified publisher should remove it and move funds to a freshly generated wallet.

stories.headline: US warns of AI-generated tooling used to attack Siemens PLCs in critical infrastructure
stories.summary: A joint advisory from the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warned that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment and other utility operators among the concerns. The agencies urged operators to remove PLCs from direct internet exposure and enforce segmentation.

stories.headline: Sakura Internet breach exposes data of up to 1.36 million accounts
stories.summary: Japanese hosting provider Sakura Internet said a hack exposed data belonging to as many as 1.36 million accounts. The company has begun notifying customers; the intrusion method has not been fully detailed publicly.

stories.headline: CareCloud breach affects 3.7 million patients
stories.summary: Healthtech company CareCloud disclosed a data breach affecting about 3.7 million patients. Health records carry a long tail of fraud risk because the data cannot be reissued the way a card number can.

stories.headline: Rogue ransomware affiliate poses as a recovery firm to intercept victims' payments
stories.summary: A group calling itself Ransom Busters claims to have hacked ransomware operators' servers and is approaching victims offering recovery for up to US$60,000. Researchers assess it as a rogue affiliate positioning itself between victims and the original crew to capture payments; paying it carries the same risks as paying the ransomware operator, plus no assurance the decryptor is genuine.

stories.headline: Spectre attack on Cloudflare Workers leaks a JWT from a co-located worker
stories.summary: Researchers demonstrated a Spectre-style side-channel against Cloudflare Workers that extracted a JSON Web Token from a different worker sharing the same isolate host, at roughly 12 bits per second. The rate is slow and the attack requires co-location, but it is a working cross-tenant leak in a serverless environment where isolation is the core security promise.

stories.headline: Four critical flaws in macOS, SharePoint, vCenter and Windows IKE added to CISA's exploited list
stories.summary: CISA added four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 18 August, all confirmed under attack: an Apple macOS authentication bypass (CVE-2026-65400, CVSS 9.8, fixed in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, Sequoia 15.7.9 and Sonoma 14.8.9), a Microsoft SharePoint weak-authentication bug (CVE-2026-55040, 9.1), a VMware vCenter Syslog path traversal leading to code execution (CVE-2026-59310, 9.8) and a double-free in the Windows IKE Extension allowing unauthenticated remote code execution (CVE-2026-33824, 9.8). These are the patches to apply first this cycle.
stories.source: The Hacker News, BleepingComputer (CISA KEV, NVD)

stories.headline: Attackers compromised more than 14,500 Dahua cameras in a 35-day campaign
stories.summary: Researchers tracked a 35-day campaign that took over more than 14,500 internet-exposed Dahua devices using credential-stuffing attacks, authentication bypasses and abuse of the vendor's peer-to-peer feature. Owners should disable P2P and remote access, change default credentials and put cameras behind a VPN.

stories.headline: SilkParasite espionage campaign hits Central Asian governments with five new RATs
stories.summary: A cyber-espionage campaign dubbed SilkParasite has targeted government bodies across Central Asia using five previously undocumented remote access trojans. Researchers describe long-dwell access focused on collection rather than disruption.

stories.headline: StopAndProtect uses nearly 2,000 hacked WordPress sites to push malware
stories.summary: A campaign tracked as StopAndProtect has compromised close to 2,000 WordPress sites and is using them to deliver malware and harvest visitor data through fake security prompts. Site owners should audit installed plugins and check for injected scripts in theme files.

stories.headline: Microsoft Copilot Personal flaws allowed one-click data exfiltration from connected apps
stories.summary: Researchers disclosed flaws in Microsoft Copilot Personal that could let a single click exfiltrate data from apps connected to the assistant. Microsoft has addressed the issues server-side; the case illustrates that connecting an assistant to mail and files widens the blast radius of any prompt-injection or link-handling bug.

stories.headline: Clop-linked web shell decrypts credentials and maps engineering data in PTC Windchill
stories.summary: A web shell tied to the Clop extortion crew has been found on PTC Windchill product-lifecycle servers, where it decrypts stored credentials and catalogues engineering data before exfiltration. Manufacturers running Windchill should hunt for unexpected JSP files and rotate any credentials the application stores.

stories.headline: US charges 17 Iranian nationals over an alleged US$3.4 billion intellectual property theft
stories.summary: The US Justice Department charged 17 Iranian nationals it links to the Mabna Institute over an alleged theft of academic and corporate data valued at US$3.4 billion, covering intrusions at universities, companies and government bodies. The defendants are not in US custody.

stories.headline: Critical GitLab GraphQL flaw let unauthenticated attackers delete public projects
stories.summary: GitLab shipped an out-of-cycle patch on 17 August for CVE-2026-19478 (CVSS 9.4), which under certain conditions let an unauthenticated attacker reaching the GraphQL endpoint modify or delete public projects and user data. Affected: CE/EE 18.2 before 18.11.11, 19.0 before 19.0.8, 19.1 before 19.1.6 and 19.2 before 19.2.4. GitLab.com and Dedicated are already patched; self-managed instances must upgrade.

stories.headline: Forminator WordPress plugin flaw enables unauthenticated remote code execution
stories.summary: CVE-2026-15748 (CVSS 9.8) affects Forminator Forms for WordPress, which has more than 600,000 active installations, in all versions up to and including 1.56.1. File-type validation in handle_file_upload() can be bypassed through a crafted upload-field configuration when a form contains both a File Upload field and a Select field, letting unauthenticated attackers upload PHP payloads. Update the plugin.

stories.headline: CISA flags an actively exploited Ray flaw that can trigger browser-based RCE
stories.summary: CISA added CVE-2025-62593 to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue on 17 August. The flaw in the Ray AI compute engine before version 2.52.0 allows remote code execution against developers using Ray as a development tool, exploitable via the browser. Upgrade to 2.52.0 or later and keep Ray dashboards off the public internet.

stories.headline: Snowflake GitHub Actions workflow could be hijacked by a crafted issue
stories.summary: Wiz disclosed a GitHub Actions workflow injection in Snowflake's snowflake-connector-net repository: a crafted GitHub issue could execute commands inside a workflow (.github/workflows/jira_issue.yml) that held internal Jira credentials. No CVE has been assigned. The pattern - untrusted issue text interpolated into a workflow run - affects many repositories, not just this one.

stories.headline: Sixteen typosquatted RubyGems packages stole browser credentials and crypto wallets
stories.summary: Sixteen malicious RubyGems packages using names close to popular libraries were found harvesting browser-stored credentials and cryptocurrency wallet files. Teams should check lockfiles for the affected names and rotate any credentials that were present on a build machine.

stories.headline: TWINLOOT abuses SharePoint and Teams to steal credentials and move across networks
stories.summary: A toolset tracked as TWINLOOT uses legitimate SharePoint and Teams functionality to harvest credentials and move laterally, blending into normal Microsoft 365 traffic. Detection depends on auditing unusual file-share and chat-app API activity rather than on network signatures.
